correctness.rationale: Perfectness gives monomial natural-basis rigidity. Comparing one weighted-cycle product under a monomial isomorphism forces the permutation to be a rotation and gives a scalar recurrence. Closing that recurrence yields one m-th-power equation with m=2^n-1. The weighted product Delta transforms under one rotation as Delta^2 modulo m-th powers, so isomorphism classes are exactly doubling orbits in the cyclic quotient of order d=gcd(m,q-1). Burnside gives the class count, the same recurrence gives d lifts for each stabilizing rotation, and the idempotent equations close to x_0^m=Delta^{-1}. The packaged checker exhaustively verifies all pairwise isomorphism decisions in several complete coefficient spaces and independently checks the class, automorphism, and idempotent counts.

originality.rationale: The 2019 graph-automorphism paper supplies the general diagonal/permutation framework for a fixed perfect evolution algebra, not an explicit finite-field classification of all weight systems on a directed cycle. The permutation-algebra literature gives cycle decompositions, sufficient isomorphism criteria, and idempotent coordinate formulas, but the accessible theorem statements do not give the quotient by m-th powers, the doubling-orbit necessity and sufficiency, the Burnside class count, or the stabilizer formula. A 2025 open full-text automorphism paper restates monomial rigidity and the graph kernel and contains no directed-cycle classification. Targeted semantic and web searches found no covering result.
residual_risks: The full Narkuziyev journal article was not available for complete inspection; an equivalent finite-field classification hidden beyond the accessible theorem summary remains possible.

value.rationale: Weighted directed cycles are the indecomposable building blocks singled out by the permutation-evolution literature, so classifying them over finite fields is structurally natural rather than an arbitrary slice. The result compresses n nonzero coefficients to one finite cyclic orbit, gives a closed count of all isomorphism classes, computes every automorphism-group order from the same orbit, and identifies the unique class supporting nonzero idempotents. The q=16,n=4 example already exhibits five classes and three distinct symmetry levels, showing that the arithmetic quotient is genuinely informative.
